Global Eugia injectable/specialty sales reached US$513 million in FY26; on an ex-gRevlimid basis Eugia grew ~12% YoY in FY26, and management guides for sustained double-digit growth in FY27.

Site transfer from Eugia-III to the new sterile Vizag facility (Eugia-V) is already underway and a majority of upcoming injectable ANDA filings are planned from Vizag, partially mitigating the Eugia-III OAI overhang.

CuraTeQ biosimilars pipeline spans 14 assets with three already launched in EU/LATAM and six in various approval stages; gross margins guided at 65-75% despite steep price erosion, offering high-quality incremental earnings once the US ramp begins.

Omalizumab Phase 3 successfully met all primary endpoints, enabling EMA and USFDA filings by end-2QCY26; Denosumab filing also targeted for 2QCY26; Pegfilgrastim targeted to generate US$50-60 million in revenue.

TheraNym Biologics CDMO secured three product agreements with MSD; Unit 2 will expand drug-substance bioreactor capacity to 60KL (~US$125 million additional capex), with revenue contribution from FY28/FY31.

Europe grew 30% YoY in 4QFY26 (EUR +11% constant currency); management guides for double-digit constant-currency growth in FY27 with EU EBITDA margins already above 20% and room to improve as China OSD supply plant scales.
Growth markets (RoW) grew 25% YoY in 4QFY26 (+18% in USD terms) driven by broad-based momentum, adding a resilient third pillar alongside the US and Europe.

Management guides for consolidated EBITDA margins to improve to 21%+ in FY27; Pen-G (Lyfius) plant at 80%+ utilization in March/April 2026 expected to break even in FY27 after a Rs2 billion+ EBITDA loss in FY26.

Highest number of pending ANDAs among Indian large-cap pharma peers; cumulative 888 ANDAs filed as of March 2026 with 728 final and 35 tentative approvals, underpinning a durable multi-year US launch pipeline.

Near-term US catalysts include gAdvair (complex inhaled generic with limited competition) and Adquey (first NCE for eczema, targeted for 2QFY27 with a dedicated dermatology commercial team), both incremental to base business guidance.
China OSD facility guided to reach profitability and double-digit EBITDA margins in FY27 vs ~US$7 million EBITDA loss in FY26, with 10+ products already launched supplying European markets.

CLSA argues the 15-20% valuation discount to large-cap pharma peers is unwarranted given industry-leading growth trajectory; brokers model ~19-20% adjusted EPS CAGR over FY26-29E as Lannett, biosimilars, Pen-G, and biologics CDMO all layer in from FY28.
India formulations guided for double-digit YoY growth in FY27, adding a domestic market tailwind alongside multiple international drivers.

The concurrent build-out of Pen-G backward integration, biosimilars commercialisation, and a biologics CDMO platform is qualitatively different from the historical commodity-generics profile — if execution holds, a structural multiple re-rating is plausible, not merely near-term earnings growth.

Lannett brings Dayton and Raleigh specialty formulation capacity (transdermal, respiratory, topical) that expands complex-product optionality beyond existing Eugia sterile lines; the long-term pipeline value may exceed the headline US$300 million revenue contribution.

downside.s: Eugia-III sterile injectable facility received OAI classification for the second consecutive inspection cycle (Feb 2024 and Feb 2026); Kotak now does not expect resolution before FY2028, blocking the 35 pending ANDAs tied to this facility.

Form 483 from the Feb 2026 Eugia-III inspection cited 11 observations including aseptic practice lapses, CCTV quality-oversight blind spots, and training deficiencies — a pattern suggesting systemic quality-culture issues rather than an isolated incident.

Eugia-III contributed ~US$125 million (3.3% of consolidated FY26 sales) including ~US$60 million of US sales; while Kotak assigns low probability to an import alert, an escalation would be an immediate and material revenue hit.
Eugia Unit I compliance response also pending from USFDA, creating two simultaneous unresolved regulatory overhangs in the injectables business.
US sales declined ~7% YoY in FY26; 4QFY26 US revenues of US$387 million missed Kotak estimates by 9% and fell 18% YoY, with the base business stable but not yet growing organically.

Persistent low- to mid-single-digit price erosion in the base US generics portfolio; biosimilars face ~60% price erosion in the US and 75-85% in the EU, compressing realisations on an accumulated US$450 million biosimilar investment since 2018.

Lannett acquisition delayed from 1QFY27 to early 2QFY27 due to a 76-day US government shutdown stalling FTC review; integrating a ~US$300 million portfolio while simultaneously ramping Dayton/Raleigh specialty lines is a meaningful execution risk.

US$450 million already invested in biosimilars since 2018 with limited revenue to date; Unit-2 biologics CDMO drug substance facility requires an additional US$150-175 million capex, raising total capital at risk in still-unproven new verticals.

Total borrowings of Rs76.8 billion in FY26; capex-to-depreciation ratio sustained above 150% as Aurobindo simultaneously funds Lannett, China, Vizag, Dayton, Pen-G, biosimilars, and biologics CDMO — free cash flow generation is structurally constrained in the near term.

New facilities in China (~US$7 million EBITDA loss in FY26), Vizag/Eugia-V, and Dayton are all currently loss-making; Pen-G posted Rs2 billion+ EBITDA loss in FY26 — these drags on consolidated margins are expected to persist at least through FY27.

TheraNym biologics CDMO is entirely dependent on a single customer (MSD) with no revenue before FY28 and Unit 1 commissioning only by end-CY2027; credibility as a CDMO for new biological entities is unproven, and scale-up risk is substantially higher than in small-molecule generics.
Persistent Eugia-III regulatory headwinds could delay or cancel the speculated Eugia subsidiary IPO, which brokers had flagged as a potential valuation re-rating catalyst for Aurobindo.

Kotak lowered FY27-29E EPS by 1-2% following the latest Eugia-III OAI and retains Reduce at FV INR 1,365 (15x FY28E PE); both Kotak and CLSA argue the stock's ~26% three-month rally has priced in the FY28 inflection, leaving limited near-term upside.

Back-to-back OAI at Eugia-III across two consecutive inspection cycles (2024 and 2026) raises concern about the depth of quality remediation; a third adverse finding or import alert would be qualitatively different from current market discounting and could de-rate the entire Eugia injectable franchise.

gRevlimid was a one-time earnings booster; the base US business was still declining (-7% in FY26), and Aurobindo needs Lannett integration, gAdvair launch, injectable ramp, and Pen-G breakeven all to execute simultaneously to reach the US$2 billion US sales target — the margin for error is thin.

With Kotak Reduce (FV 1,365), CLSA Hold (TP 1,490), and only Goldman Sachs at Buy (TP 1,550, ~6% premium to CMP), consensus is mildly negative; FY28 is the consensus inflection year, meaning current multiples are elevated and the stock needs to deliver on multiple concurrent execution risks before re-rating.

upside.s: FY26 revenue consensus estimate raised 17% over 12 months and 4% in the past 3 months — the strongest positive revision in the Indian EMS cohort, ahead of Syrma (−2%), Dixon (−13%), Kaynes (−20%), and Amber (+5%), signalling improving execution credibility.

4QFY26 revenue of ₹4,799mn grew 40% YoY — materially above EMS peers Amber (10%), Dixon (2%), and Kaynes (26%) — reflecting differentiated end-market exposure to power electronics, medical, and aerospace rather than commodity consumer appliances.

FY26 PAT consensus revised up 14% over 12 months and 6% in the past quarter — one of very few EMS names with positive PAT revisions in a year when Amber (−23%), Dixon (−36%), and Kaynes (−27%) all saw double-digit estimate cuts.

EBITDA margin of 11.8% in 4QFY26 is materially higher than Dixon (3.9%) and Amber (8.6%) and comparable to Syrma (11.9%), reflecting a differentiated, technically complex product mix rather than commodity appliance assembly.

Assembly-focused EMS business model benefits from a commodity cost pass-through pricing mechanism, limiting direct earnings exposure to copper and aluminium price spikes — CLSA notes this provides structural margin protection relative to backward-integrated peers where cost pass-through involves a greater lag.

US manufacturing footprint makes Avalon one of the very few Indian EMS players able to serve American OEMs in defence, aerospace, and medical — segments that often require US-domiciled manufacturing, ITAR compliance, or domestic content provisions — creating a near-zero-competitor moat among Indian-listed EMS peers.

Specialisation in power electronics, clean energy, semiconductor, medical, and aerospace OEM assembly creates high certification barriers and long qualification cycles; once qualified, customer switching costs are very high and relationships are inherently sticky — a durability characteristic absent from mass-consumer-appliance EMS.

Sector-wide EMS margin accretion is expected as players shift toward higher-margin product categories and deepen backward integration; Avalon's already-premium margins (11.8% vs 3.9%–8.6% for Dixon/Amber) suggest it is ahead of this curve rather than a beneficiary waiting to arrive.

downside.s: Despite 40% YoY revenue growth in 4QFY26, EBITDA margin contracted 22bps YoY to 11.8% — the margin expansion story is not unambiguously positive; scale-up costs are absorbing some top-line momentum.

Stock returned 47% in 3 months and 71% over 12 months — by far the strongest performer in the EMS cohort tracked by CLSA — raising risk that valuation re-rating is already fully captured and near-term estimate upgrades have been priced in.

Broader EMS sector demand remained soft in 4QFY26 per CLSA's sector-wide review; commodity inflation and weak discretionary spending are sector-wide headwinds that also apply to Avalon's customer base.

Continued rises in input costs (copper, aluminium) can weigh on earnings if commodity inflation persists; the pass-through model protects assembly margins but does not prevent customers from deferring orders under cost pressure.

At ~₹4.8bn quarterly revenue (~₹19bn annualised run-rate), Avalon is among the smallest listed EMS players — Dixon is ~22x larger, Amber ~9x larger. Small scale amplifies earnings volatility from individual contract wins or losses, and large OEMs may preference bigger, better-resourced peers for high-volume production mandates.

US manufacturing operations carry a structural cost headwind: US labour and overhead are multiples of India's equivalent, so the US business must generate substantially higher per-unit margins to avoid diluting the blended group EBITDA margin — US profitability is undisclosed and is a key unknown in the investment thesis.

Concentration in power electronics, defence, aerospace, and medical creates project-based, lumpy revenue — unlike mass-consumer-appliance supply, these segments feature extended qualification lead times, programme cancellations, and multi-year budget cycles that can cause abrupt quarterly revenue swings with little advance warning.

Very sparse sell-side coverage (only comparative data-points identified in the sector notebook, no standalone initiations found) means consensus estimates rest on a thin analytical base — mispricing in either direction is more likely than for heavily-covered EMS peers, and estimate stability is less reliable.

upside.s: Jefferies' base case builds in 23% AUM CAGR over FY26-29; the upside scenario sees 24% CAGR, driving a SoTP-derived price target of Rs2,640 vs a base PT of Rs1,210 — implying the bull-bear spread is tight, which is actually reassuring: even in the bear case Jefferies still sees only -12% downside (PT Rs1,540).

Management guides for 22-24% AUM growth in FY27 and 23-25% over the medium term; Kotak models 22% (lower-end) while Jefferies models 23% CAGR — both above consensus for most large NBFCs, underscoring BAF's structural volume advantage in under-penetrated consumer and SME segments.

Credit cost guide of 145-160bps for FY27 (vs ~205bps actuals in FY26) implies a 15-30bps improvement; if achieved, the combined effect of lower provisions + operating leverage can drive >30% FY27 PAT growth on a low base — consensus already expects 33% EPS growth in FY27.

Asset quality has recovered sharply: GNPA at 1.01% and NNPA at 0.41% as of 4QFY26, well off earlier stress levels; provision coverage has been rebuilt after an accelerated ECL overlay in 3QFY26, removing the near-term fear of a sustained provisioning cycle.

The wind-down of captive 2W/3W financing (now <1% of the portfolio, expected to fall to <Rs15bn AUM by Sep 2026) eliminates a drag that had suppressed overall vehicle-financing portfolio growth for multiple quarters — removing this headwind alone mechanically improves reported AUM growth.

MSME/Business Loan portfolio, which decelerated to just 6% growth by Mar 2026, is expected to recover starting 2Q-3QFY27 aided by a favourable base effect; Stage 2/3 assets in the BL book have already been sequentially reduced and vintage credit performance is showing significant improvement.

Newer segments — MFI and gold loans — now account for ~5% of the total portfolio and are growing rapidly; gold loan and tractor loan scale-up without impacting profitability is Bernstein's own stated upside risk even from an Underperform stance.

Management guided for 25-40bps cost ratio improvement driven by operating leverage and AI; the Bajaj Finserv group is cited by Jefferies as among the biggest consumers of compute power of global tech platforms, using AI to both reduce costs and lift revenues — a differentiator vs most Indian NBFC peers.

Bajaj Housing Finance (87% stake) delivered 23% AUM growth in 4QFY26 with negligible credit costs of 16bps, providing a clean, fast-growing mortgage subsidiary that diversifies group earnings away from unsecured lending; Jefferies values the BHFL stake at Rs636bn (Rs102/share) in its BAF SoTP.

Jefferies and Kotak both carried BAF as a top NBFC sector pick as of May 2026, with ROE tracking 18-20% on Kotak's estimates — among the highest risk-adjusted return profiles in the listed NBFC universe, justifying a premium multiple over peers.

RBI rate easing cycle provides a structural tailwind: accelerated and deeper-than-anticipated rate cuts would boost NIMs, reduce credit stress in the unsecured book, and support faster MSME recovery — all three transmission channels benefit BAF simultaneously.

The FY27 earnings recovery story is consensus-supported with limited execution risk on the near-term credit cost guide: even Bernstein (the bear) models 30% EPS growth in FY27, creating a rare situation where the bull-bear debate is about long-term normalisation rather than near-term delivery.

downside.s: Kotak bakes in 40bps NIM compression in FY27 and a further 20bps in FY28 to account for elevated competitive intensity — the magnitude implies NIMs could fall from already-modest levels, structurally reducing the spread that drives BAF's superior ROA versus peers.

Marginal cost of funds has risen 10-15bps across NBFCs (flagged by BAF and peers including CIFC) — asset yields in competitive segments like consumer durables and personal loans are repricing down faster than funding costs are easing, compressing NIM from both sides.

BAF's large share of unsecured lending makes its book disproportionately vulnerable to a macro shock: a prolonged West Asia conflict, fiscal slippage, or elevated bond yields could reignite credit stress in the small-ticket unsecured book that had barely stabilised after the FY25-26 cycle.

Bernstein maintains Underperform with a Rs840 target (21x FY27E EPS), arguing BAF's long-term earnings growth will normalise below 20% once the FY27 credit-cost tailwind fades — the current ~25x forward multiple demands a sustained high-teens-to-20% CAGR that Bernstein views as unlikely given structural credit penetration limits.

BAF has been in a two-year consensus EPS downgrade cycle: FY26 EPS estimates fell 12% and FY28 estimates fell 13% from Aug 2024 peaks — Bernstein warns any macro deterioration could extend this cycle, particularly given the elevated cost and credit-cost base relative to pre-COVID levels.

Jio Financial Services' aggressive expansion into consumer lending is an identified structural threat — Jio FS has the distribution reach, Jio customer data advantage, and Reliance balance-sheet to undercut BAF on rates in consumer durables and personal loans, BAF's highest-volume categories.

Despite the accelerated ECL overlay in 3QFY26 rebuilding provision coverage, structurally higher slippages and write-offs persist relative to pre-COVID levels — front-loaded provisioning provides temporary relief but does not resolve the underlying question of whether the steady-state credit cost for BAF's unsecured book has durably risen.

Recent opex efficiency gains appear driven by calibrated cost control (slower branch expansion, lower cost per employee) rather than structural productivity gains from AI — as BAF accelerates expansion into lower-operating-leverage segments like MFI and gold loans, the recent opex-to-AUM improvement may reverse.

India's non-mortgage household credit penetration is already high relative to GDP and regional peers — Bernstein argues BAF is unlikely to sustain AUM growth materially above system credit growth without yield compression or a move into riskier segments, capping long-term upside surprises.

A rising frequency of one-time P&L adjustments (accelerated ECL charges, BHFL IPO gains) over FY25-26 has complicated true underlying earnings comparability — Bernstein explicitly flags this as an early warning of weakening franchise strength, drawing parallels to post-merger HDFC Bank.

Bajaj Housing Finance NIM compressed 24bps YoY to 3.12% in 4QFY26; as BHFL grows as a share of consolidated AUM (23% growth rate vs the parent's ~22%), it will dilute blended group NIMs and ROA — the subsidiary is strategically valuable but is structurally a margin drag on the consolidated entity.

The three analysts in the notebook show a Rs370 spread in target prices (Rs840–Rs1,210) on the same set of published numbers — this unusual dispersion signals that BAF's intrinsic value is genuinely hard to anchor and that the 'correct' long-term normalised credit cost and growth rate are still unsettled consensus questions.

upside.s: Bajaj Finance AUM grew 22% YoY to ₹5.1tn in 4QFY26 with credit costs falling 52bps YoY to 1.7%, signaling a decisive recovery from the prior consumer-lending stress cycle.
BALIC (life insurance) VNB surged 29% YoY to ₹7.09bn in 4QFY26, with VNB margin expanding 237bps YoY to 24% — strong value-accretive growth showing BALIC is improving in the right product segments.

Bajaj Finance's cross-sell franchise as a % of total customer base rose steadily from 48% in FY15 to 63% in FY26, a compounding retention-driven advantage that structurally reduces customer acquisition costs.

NBFCs like Bajaj Finance dominate small-ticket, high-yield, new-to-credit lending with tailored operating models (distribution, underwriting, collections) that banks cannot structurally replicate — a durable right-to-win in a segment with low competitive overlap.
New ventures (payments, broking, AMC) are near breakeven per Jefferies May 2026 roadshow feedback, meaning the current P&L drag on consolidated ROE is close to inflecting into a net contribution.
Healthcare segment is actively ramping up, adding a new growth vertical that extends Bajaj Finserv's franchise beyond core NBFC and insurance.
Jefferies rates Bajaj Finserv BUY with TP ₹2,400, implying 39–41% upside from May–June 2026 levels, calling it a top pick in diversified financials on healthy growth in core consolidated profits.

BJFIN trades at a significant discount to SOTP of its subsidiaries; a re-rating catalyst exists if new ventures reach profitability or the holding company discount compresses in a broader diversified-financials re-rating cycle.

BALIC's VNB margin trajectory (22% FY25 → 24% 4QFY26) and EV growth of ~6% YoY suggest the life insurance arm is structurally improving on value metrics that predict long-run value creation better than near-term premium volumes.

downside.s: Bernstein rates Bajaj Finance (BJFIN's primary profit engine) Underperform with TP ₹840 vs ~₹923 market price, citing 29x FY26 P/B as too rich; BAF valuation risk flows directly through to the consolidated parent.

BAGIC (general insurance) combined ratio spiked to 113.6% in 4QFY26 (+874bps YoY, +1,571bps QoQ), meaning the subsidiary paid out more in claims and expenses than it collected in premiums — a sharp sequential deterioration.

Allianz (Bajaj's own strategic partner) formed a 50:50 JV with Jio Financial for general and life insurance, creating a well-funded direct competitor to BAGIC and BALIC backed by the same global insurer that built the Bajaj franchise.

IRDAI approved Ind AS 17 (IFRS 17) from April 1, 2026 with two years of parallel reporting — introducing P&L volatility and potential capital requirement changes for both BALIC and BAGIC with limited Indian market precedent.

Bond yield spikes are expected to have a greater negative impact on NBFC margins than on banks per Bernstein — directly compressing Bajaj Finance's NIM and, by extension, BJFIN's consolidated earnings.

New ventures (payments, broking, AMC) remain ROE-dilutive drag on consolidated returns; 'near breakeven' as of the May 2026 roadshow still means net losses with no quantified timeline to profitability.

As a holding company, BJFIN structurally trades at a discount to SOTP — investors cannot directly access subsidiary cash flows and the multi-subsidiary complexity creates valuation opacity unlikely to fully close.

Bajaj Finance contributes the overwhelming majority of BJFIN's consolidated profits; any credit cost cycle reversal, regulatory action on consumer lending, or competitive commoditization of the NBFC underwriting model disproportionately impacts the entire Bajaj Finserv franchise.
IRDAI linked insurer executive pay to elimination of unfair insurer-hospital practices (50% of KPIs now mandatory) — adding compliance complexity and operational overhead for both BALIC and BAGIC.

Credit card sector showed a weak start to FY27 with subdued spends and issuances in April 2026; JPMorgan notes diversified bank issuers are structurally better positioned than mono-line players, posing a headwind to BAF's growing credit card and EMI book.

upside.s: Jefferies projects 26% EBITDA CAGR and 30% EPS CAGR over FY26-28E, with manufacturing revenues growing 16% in FY27E and 28% in FY28E (partly lifted by group entity BAPL/EITSPL merger accretion).

Two new OEM order wins (likely TVS and a Japanese OEM) for exhaust systems and fuel tanks start production in 2QFY27 and 4QFY27, adding ~Rs 3 billion in annual revenue on full ramp-up (~3% of FY26 revenues).

Strong balance sheet post-IPO: net debt/EBITDA of only 0.1x in FY26, and net interest expense fell 53% YoY in 4QFY26 as IPO proceeds retired debt; leaves capacity for the capex plan without leverage risk.

EBITDA margins expected to expand from 12.1% in FY26 to 13.5% by FY28E; Belrise has historically delivered stable margins in a tight 12-14% band over FY21-26, suggesting the expansion trajectory is credible.

Aerospace/defense diversification via France (SDM) and UK acquisitions enters the global aerospace components supply chain; strategic agreement with an Israeli firm opens defense opportunities — modest near-term but meaningful medium-term re-rating catalyst.

Rising content-per-vehicle in a premiumising 2W segment and growing 4W exposure (32% and 70% growth in CV and PV revenues respectively in 4QFY26 from low base) broadens the revenue mix beyond core 2Ws.
Bull-case scenario offers 35% upside (Rs 285 PT) on manufacturing revenue growing 32% in FY28E and EBITDA margins reaching 14.1% by FY29E.

The group entity merger in FY28 is a relatively visible, near-term earnings catalyst; BAPL/EITSPL consolidation adds ~Rs 14.1 billion in manufacturing revenue and is not contingent on new customer wins — the market may not be fully pricing this yet.

With 4W revenues still only ~10% of total, Belrise has substantial runway to deepen penetration with PV and CV OEMs — a structural growth path that could sustain double-digit revenue growth beyond FY28 even without the merger boost.

downside.s: High customer concentration: top customer (believed to be Bajaj Auto) dominates the revenue base; any Bajaj-specific volume weakness or pricing renegotiation would disproportionately impact Belrise.
~65% of revenues from 2W components exposes Belrise to cyclical downturns in domestic 2W demand; a slowdown in the segment would have an outsized earnings impact.

Structural EV risk to exhaust systems: Belrise holds ~24% market share in key products including exhaust systems, which are obsolete in battery EVs; rising 2W EV penetration will gradually erode this revenue pool.
Margin headwinds from commodity prices, fuel, and transportation costs: EBITDA margin contracted 90bp QoQ to 11.4% in 4QFY26; bear-case assumes margins stay at 11.0% in FY27E vs 12.0% base case.
Trading revenues (~20% of top line, largely commodity pass-through) are volatile and fell 21% YoY in 4QFY26, dragging total revenue growth from 21% manufacturing to 12% consolidated.

Aerospace/defense diversification is at inception: SDM acquisition incurred Rs 95 million in one-time start-up/integration costs (40bp revenue impact in 4QFY26); further integration risk and delayed ramp-up could weigh on near-term margins.

Jefferies' downside scenario implies a 13% decline to Rs 183 (25x Mar-28E EPS) on revenue growing only 9%/19%/7% over FY27-29E and margins compressing to 11.0-12.5%; the base case offers limited margin for error.

At 29x FY27E PE, valuation is front-loaded: much of the premium depends on the FY28 merger accretion and successful aerospace ramp. Any execution slip — whether in integration, new order ramp, or a 2W cycle miss — could trigger sharp multiple compression from the elevated starting PE.

The aerospace/defense angle is optionality, not yet an earnings driver — the Israeli JV was just announced and SDM only expected to turn profitable in FY27. There is a risk the market prices in diversification before it delivers, setting up for a narrative unwind if integration timelines stretch.
